prior_art.edition: Official Records I vol. 39 pt. 2 p. 524 (civilwar.com page 221025-524, fetched 4 Nov 2026) prints the message: 'HEADQUARTERS DEPARTMENT OF THE OHIO, Knoxville, Tenn., September 29, 1864. Brigadier-General AMMEN ... You will get the following order through to General Burbridge ... Recall General Burbridge, with his forces, to come to this city or the nearest convenient point on the Louisville and Nashville Railroad. W. T. SHERMAN, By J. D. WEBSTER ... Acknowledge receipt and report as soon as General Burbridge has received the order. I do not know that he has this. By command of Major-General Schofield: G. M. BASCOM'. These are the words on the leaf, so its plaintext is on record.
prior_art.literature: Web searches for the letter with Ammen, Stager, cipher found no study, but the OR text above settles the content; the leaf is a transposition of that message with a 'Friend General' salutation and null words.
